title: APPO: Agentic Procedural Policy Optimization
title_zh: APPO：智能体式过程策略优化
abstract_en: Recent advances in agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL) have substantially improved the multi-turn tool-use capabilities of large language model agents. However, most existing methods assign credit over coarse heuristic units, such as tool-call boundaries or fixed workflows, making it difficult to identify which intermediate decisions influence downstream outcomes. In this work, we study agentic RL from two perspectives: \textit{where to branch and how to assign credit after branching}. Our pilot analysis shows that influential decision points are broadly distributed throughout the generated sequence rather than concentrated at tool calls, while token entropy alone does not reliably reflect their impact on final outcomes. Motivated by these observations, we propose \textbf{Agentic Procedural Policy Optimization (APPO)}, which shifts branching and credit assignment from coarse interaction units to fine-grained decision points in the sequence. APPO selects branching locations using a Branching Score that combines token uncertainty with policy-induced likelihood gains of subsequent continuations, enabling more targeted exploration while filtering out spurious high-entropy positions. It further introduces procedure-level advantage scaling to better distribute credit across branched rollouts. Experiments on 13 benchmarks show that APPO consistently improves strong agentic RL baselines by nearly 4 points, while keeping efficient tool-calls and maintaining behavior interpretability.
abstract_zh: 近期 agentic Reinforcement Learning（RL）显著提升了大语言模型智能体的多轮工具使用能力。然而，现有方法多在工具调用边界或固定工作流等粗粒度启发式单元上分配信用，难以识别哪些中间决策真正影响最终结果。本文从“在哪里分支”与“分支后如何分配信用”两个角度研究 agentic RL。初步分析发现，关键决策点广泛分布在生成序列中，并不集中于工具调用位置；同时，单纯的 token entropy 也无法可靠反映其对最终结果的影响。基于此，作者提出 Agentic Procedural Policy Optimization（APPO），将分支探索与信用分配从粗粒度交互单元推进到序列中的细粒度决策点。APPO 通过 Branching Score 选择分支位置，该分数结合 token 不确定性与后续 continuation 的策略诱导似然增益，从而更有针对性地探索，并过滤掉虚假的高熵位置。此外，APPO 引入 procedure-level advantage scaling，以更合理地在分支 rollout 间分配信用。在 13 个 benchmark 上，APPO 相比强 agentic RL baseline 稳定提升近 4 分，同时保持较高工具调用效率与行为可解释性。
key_points_zh: 问题定位：现有 agentic RL 往往按工具调用边界或固定流程进行粗粒度信用分配，难以精确判断哪些中间 token 级决策影响最终任务成败。
核心发现：有影响力的决策点并不只出现在 tool-call 附近，而是广泛分布于生成序列；仅依赖 token entropy 选择探索位置会引入大量伪高熵点。
方法贡献：APPO 使用 Branching Score 结合 token uncertainty 与后续 continuation 的 policy-induced likelihood gains，选择更有价值的细粒度分支点。
信用分配：提出 procedure-level advantage scaling，在分支 rollout 之间更合理地传播和缩放优势信号，改善长程、多步智能体行为的优化。
实验结果：在 13 个 benchmarks 上，APPO 相比强 agentic RL baselines 平均提升接近 4 分，同时保持高效 tool-call 使用与较好的行为可解释性。

llm_assessment.comment: A solid agentic RL method for finer-grained branching and credit assignment, though less directly tied to production harness governance.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 该工作提出了较扎实的智能体强化学习方法，用于更细粒度的分支探索和信用分配，但与生产级治理基础设施关联较弱。
